methodology: Five consecutive verses screened individually; direct Qur'an Arabic 12:86 and 12:90 plus English context and Genesis 42/45 English primary translation read. Comparisons distinguish scenes from motifs; no borrowing or direct dependence inferred. Preliminary, not critical-edition verified.

assessments.subject: Jacob directs grief to God
assessments.evidence: Genesis 42:36–38 portrays Jacob's grief but does not record this direct theological declaration.

assessments.subject: Jacob sends sons to seek Joseph and Benjamin
assessments.evidence: Genesis sends brothers to Egypt to buy food and withholds Benjamin; it does not narrate a search for both missing sons.

assessments.subject: Brothers plead poverty and request full measure
assessments.evidence: Both narrate a family seeking food in famine; Genesis 42 does not contain this specific appeal for charitable full measure.

assessments.subject: Joseph asks brothers to recall past treatment
assessments.evidence: Genesis has brothers themselves recall their wrongdoing while Joseph listens unrecognized; Qur'an has Joseph challenge them directly.

assessments.subject: Brothers recognize Joseph; Joseph invokes divine favor and patience
assessments.relationship: close recognition scene with theological difference
assessments.evidence: Genesis depicts Joseph announcing his identity and attributing events to God's preservation plan; Qur'an has brothers ask his identity and Joseph emphasize patience and piety.

dossier.title: Joseph's disclosure and his brothers' return during famine
dossier.comparative_summary: Qur'an 12:86–90 progresses from Jacob's faith and search instruction to the brothers' request for grain, Joseph's confrontation and recognition. Genesis 42 depicts an earlier famine journey, while Genesis 45 records Joseph disclosing himself and crediting divine providence. The accounts share family recognition but arrange dialogue and theological emphasis differently.

source_table.edition: Quran.com Arabic and Mustafa Khattab English

dossier.chronological_background: Genesis is a pre-Islamic scriptural tradition. Date of literary formation, textual redaction, translation and surviving manuscript witnesses must be distinguished; none assigned precisely in this preliminary pass.
variant_witnesses_pending: Masoretic Hebrew critical text and apparatus
dossier.scholarly_interpretations: Common Joseph narrative heritage is plausible; precise transmission and dependence are unproven. Compare later Jewish and Syriac retellings in a dedicated verification pass.
